open-question.question: Where, and at what length, does the README explain the name Gurita? The naming draft holds that the name says nothing to most English speakers and that its meaning, Indonesian for octopus with the plugin as the arms that each carry a mission out on their own, should be one sentence away on the landing page. The README today explains no name: its "Why Cairn?" section is about handing long-running work to an agent, not about the word.
open-question.alternative: The root README carries one sentence on the name in the block directly under the title, beside the tagline and the pitch and above the diagram: Gurita is Indonesian for octopus, and the plugin is the arms, each carrying a mission out on its own. Nothing else in the README explains the name, the "Why" section stays about the handoff, and the host READMEs carry no explanation. It does exactly what the naming draft asks, the meaning one sentence away at the first point of contact, and the sentence doubles as a description of what the plugin does, so it costs the pitch little. It adds a third line to the densest part of the page, between title and diagram, and how it reads there depends on whether the tagline above it stays, which the README tagline question owns; a second image line next to an unchanged stone tagline would clash.

The root README glosses the name inside its opening pitch with a bare translation, a parenthetical such as "Gurita (Indonesian for octopus) brings all the important questions up…", and nothing more: no image of the arms, no section of its own, the "Why" section left about the handoff, and the three host READMEs unchanged beyond the plain rename. The cheapest possible answer to the draft's "one sentence away": the word is explained at the first place a reader meets it, with no added line on a landing page whose top is already badges, a traffic table, the title, the tagline, the pitch, and a diagram. It translates the word but drops the reason the name was chosen, the arms that each carry a mission out on their own, so the name reads as an arbitrary animal; and a "Why Gurita?" heading further down, if the section keeps that title, promises a name explanation it does not give.

The root README's "Why Cairn?" section is retitled "Why Gurita?" and opens with one sentence on the name (Indonesian for octopus, the plugin as the arms that each carry a mission out on their own), its existing paragraphs on handing long-running work to an agent following unchanged. The top of the page and the host READMEs carry no explanation. It makes the heading mean what it says, a reader asking "why this name?" finds the answer under the question, and it leads straight into the section's existing argument, since independent arms is the handoff that section describes; the top of the page stays as it is. The section sits below installation, so a reader who stops at the pitch or goes straight to the install commands never meets the meaning, which is further than the draft's "one sentence away"; and it mixes a note on the word into a section about a problem and its approach.

The root README gains a short section of its own on the name, such as "## The name", placed below the "Why" section or near the foot of the page: a paragraph saying Gurita is Indonesian and Malay for octopus, how it is pronounced (gu-RI-ta), and why the image fits, an octopus's arms each sensing and acting on their own while the head sets the goal, as a mission resolves its own questions and runs beside others. The pitch block and the "Why" section carry no explanation, and the host READMEs none. It gives the name the room to land as a design statement, carrying the pronunciation and the arms-and-head image the draft records, without touching the pitch or the handoff argument. The longest explanation stands furthest from the first mention, so the reader who most needs the gloss reaches it last or never; and a paragraph on the image is prose that ages with the design it describes and leans on the orchestrator's head that ideas/kepala.md has not yet made real.

The root README carries both: one sentence on the name in the pitch block under the title (Indonesian for octopus, the plugin as the arms that each carry a mission out), and a short paragraph further down, in its own section or opening the retitled "Why Gurita?" section, adding the pronunciation and why the image fits. The host READMEs carry no explanation. The skimming reader gets the meaning at once and the curious one the reasoning, each at the depth they want, which is the fullest answer to both "one sentence away" and the empty name explanation the README has today. The name is explained twice on one page, the paragraph partly restating the sentence, and it adds the most prose of any option to a README that is otherwise about what the plugin does; the pitch-block line also depends on the tagline's fate, which the README tagline question owns.

One sentence on the name, Indonesian for octopus with the plugin as the arms that each carry a mission out on their own, stands in the pitch block under the title of the root README and of each of the three host README templates under scripts/hosts/, rendered into every hosts/ tree and published to each distribution repository; no longer explanation anywhere. Claude Code users are pointed at the distribution repository as the recommended source, so many first meet the name on a host README rather than the root one; this puts the meaning one sentence away on every landing page a reader can arrive at. The sentence is written four times in four files that can drift apart, and the host READMEs are deliberately short distribution notes; it widens the change beyond the one README the question names, and how the host READMEs open also depends on what they say of the former name, which the former-name question owns.

No README explains the name: the root README and the host READMEs say Gurita wherever they said Cairn, the "Why" section stays about the handoff under a heading that does not ask about the word, and the meaning stays recorded only in the naming draft, ideas/gurita.md, as Cairn's meaning was never stated on the landing page. It keeps the README entirely about what the plugin does and how to install it, adds nothing to maintain, and matches how the page treated the old name, which explained no word either. It goes against the naming draft's stated intent, and the rename is exactly when readers who knew the plugin as Cairn arrive asking what the new word is; a name that says nothing to most English speakers, with no gloss anywhere a user looks, reads as arbitrary and is harder to remember and spell.
